title: Route social Cat II targets after adjudication
description: D&D Cat II social resolutions currently end the beat after scoped pressure facts, which lets the resolver decide NPC outcomes instead of letting affected agents react. Use existing next_output routing for affected social targets and add prompt guidance to keep social successes as scoped framing rather than NPC decisions.
close_reason: Implemented social Cat II follow-up routing and prompt guidance

title: Spawn hidden Cat II responders before dispatching to them
description: During the mill approach in cli_long_dnd_social_20260520, the router opened a Cat II Stealth/Investigation contest with required responders brigand_lookout_1 and brigand_lookout_2. The dispatcher immediately warned that both ids were unknown, then character_manager spawned Dace Merrow and Thorne Vex afterward. This ordering means required responder ids can be routed before the corresponding character records and agents exist.
acceptance_criteria: If a Cat II event requires newly discovered or hidden NPC responders, those character records exist before any responder dispatch attempts; otherwise the router must not put unresolved ids in required_responders. The warning path for unknown required responders should be eliminated or treated as a contract failure.
close_reason: Implemented: Cat II required responder spawns are materialized before responder dispatch; unresolved required responder ids now fail loudly.

title: Support universal D&D combat actions like Dodge
description: In CLI playtest cli_takeover_haiku_20260520, after manually starting combat, Garrick's turn text 'I take the Dodge action...' reached dnd_combat_manager, which planned source_type='action' source_id='dodge'. Validation then raised ValueError: D&D combat action source is not available on the actor: actor='player_protagonist' source_type='action' source_id='dodge'. Dodge is a universal 5e combat action and should not require D&D Beyond to list it as a sheet action. Acceptance: Dodge/Disengage/Dash/Help/Hide/Ready/Search/Use Object style baseline actions resolve without internal errors, advance initiative appropriately, and surface visible/combat-state results where relevant.
close_reason: Added standard D&D combat actions for Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Ready, Search, and Use an Object, updated combat-manager prompt guidance, and covered no-roll validation with tests.

title: Surface missing D&D combat manager API key cleanly
description: CLI playtest session cli_takeover_haiku_20260520 hit an internal error when a combat turn first invoked dnd_combat_manager. Router and narrator had role keys, but dnd_combat_manager had no OpenAI key; verbose repro logged: openai.OpenAIError: The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable. Acceptance: combat setup or first combat action detects missing dnd_combat_manager credentials with a clear CLI-facing configuration error, or role-key fallback/config docs make this impossible in normal local playtests.
notes:
Reopened after review: router-key fallback is incorrect because all role keys should be loaded from the same shell environment. Remove fallback and fix exact role env loading instead.
Follow-up correction: do not load role keys from ~/.bashrc at runtime. Keep the explicit combat-manager key contract and put OPEN_AI_COMBAT_MANAGER in the local gitignored .env instead.
close_reason: Simplified the combat-manager key fix: removed the ~/.bashrc LLM env loader, kept the no-router-fallback behavior, verified .env provides OPEN_AI_COMBAT_MANAGER locally, and preserved tests for the explicit role-key contract.

Fix the provider schema normalizer, tighten the event-router agent-output contract, verify with focused tests, and rerun the affected CLI path.

title: Add narrator-only name obfuscation harness

The harness must not run router, agent, combat manager, or full turn-loop LLM calls.

Initial probe exposed resolver-leaked Dace/Thorne labels; narrator prompt now treats unquoted proper-name labels as non-viewpoint knowledge, and the live narrator probe passes all three cases.

title: Align narrator prompt with per-viewpoint naming contract
description: The narrator role has evolved from whole-scene renderer to per-player POV renderer. Tighten narrator_phase2.txt so it consistently describes one viewpoint passage, keeps names constrained to what that viewpoint can know, and reconciles raw-id display fallback with name obfuscation for unintroduced characters.
acceptance_criteria: narrator_phase2.txt consistently describes one listed viewpoint, does not imply omniscient scene rendering, and tells the narrator to use visible descriptions rather than names when a character is not introduced to that viewpoint.
close_reason: Aligned narrator_phase2 prompt wording with per-viewpoint rendering and name-knowledge boundaries; focused narrator and prompt hygiene tests pass.

title: Route consequences when hidden observers beat player Stealth
description: In cli_long_dnd_social_20260520, Garrick rolled Stealth 12 while Dace's opposed Perception was 13. The checkpoint recorded that Dace noticed and could track him, while Thorne did not. The player-facing beat then returned control without an immediate lookout reaction or clear consequence; the next pressure only happened because the player manually spoke toward the hedge. At a D&D table, a failed stealth contest against a hidden lookout usually changes the fiction immediately: the watcher warns, freezes, readies a shot, signals, or otherwise acts on the information.
acceptance_criteria: When a hidden observer succeeds against a player's stealth/recon approach, resolution either routes that observer for an immediate response or narrates a concrete consequence/state change that preserves the observer's agency and gives the players an actionable new situation.

title: Reconcile attached D&D sheet equipment with story fiction
description: In cli_long_dnd_social_20260520, Garrick and Lyra were attached from sample D&D sheets. /sheet and /inventory showed canonical D&D equipment such as chain mail, shield, longsword, scale mail, mace, and holy symbol, while the story fiction treated them as just-arrived unblessed characters being outfitted by Korva from spare kit. From a D&D play perspective this makes AC, encumbrance, disadvantage, weapons, and gear authority confusing: the mechanics say one loadout exists, the scene says another loadout is being granted.
acceptance_criteria: Takeover attachment has a clear policy for imported equipment: either render sheet equipment as physically present in the scene, mark imported loadout as unavailable/template-only until fiction grants it, or reconcile it during attachment/start so sheet, inventory, and narration agree.
close_reason: Completed: tightened D&D narrative loot fallback/display and made attached sheet equipment current gear in D&D player context.

title: Tighten D&D narrative loot inference and offer display
description: The long CLI playtest found both useful and bad loot behavior. Korva's spare kit produced a structured offer, but /loot showed labels like 'scaled vest (armor) (armor)' and the remaining offer stayed open for the leftover shortsword. Worse, mundane fiction produced false loot offers: Korva gathering a lead rope for a supply mule created a stable hand rope offer, and Garrick pulling rope from his own pack to restrain Dace created duplicate narrative handoff rope offers. The fallback should not infer loot from tack, existing inventory use, or ordinary handling of owned gear.
acceptance_criteria: Narrative loot fallback only creates offers for newly offered/takeable items; using an owned item or animal tack does not create a new offer; armor/gear labels are not duplicated; partially claimed offers present only genuinely remaining items and avoid stale duplicate prompts.
close_reason: Completed: tightened D&D narrative loot fallback/display and made attached sheet equipment current gear in D&D player context.

title: Make pending player rolls easy to resolve after multi-PC Cat II pauses
description: In cli_long_dnd_social_20260520, Garrick initiated Stealth/Investigation and later Intimidation checks. The Cat II pause switched control to Lyra for her responder input, then the pending rolls still belonged to Garrick while the current CLI actor remained Lyra. Running /roll all printed 'no pending D&D roll for the current actor' until manually switching back with /as player_protagonist. This is awkward for multiplayer takeover play and makes the roll affordance feel broken even when pending rolls exist.
acceptance_criteria: When any claimed player character has pending D&D rolls after a Cat II pause, the CLI either auto-selects that character, lets /roll all resolve all eligible claimed-player pending rolls, or clearly lists which actor has pending rolls and the exact command to switch/roll.

title: Hide NPC opposed roll totals from player-facing CLI output
description: Long D&D CLI playtest cli_long_dnd_social_20260520 exposed NPC opposed rolls before the player rolled: Korva Deception vs Lyra, Dace/Thorne Perception against Garrick Stealth, and Dace/Thorne Insight against Garrick Intimidation/Deception. From a D&D table perspective this leaks target competence, awareness, and social read state before the player knows the result. Keep the mechanical ledger internally, but make the player-facing interactive-roll flow either hide NPC totals until the outcome is narrated or show a non-spoiling pending/opposed indicator.
acceptance_criteria: Player-facing CLI and Discord roll displays do not reveal NPC opposed social/stealth roll totals before the relevant player roll resolves; completed outcomes still have enough audit/debug data in logs or checkpoint transactions.

title: Make CLI combat participant selection work from visible NPC names
description: In CLI playtest cli_takeover_haiku_20260520, the narrative introduced the brigand leader to the player as Herrik Voss. Attempting /combat begin player_protagonist,player_protagonist_2,herrik_voss failed with Unknown combat participant(s): herrik_voss, while the checkpoint had the spawned character id brigand_leader_herrik. From the CLI player's POV, visible names and command ids diverge at the exact moment combat might start. Acceptance: CLI either accepts unambiguous display-name/name slugs for combat participant refs or surfaces the actual character_id in /characters or the relevant prompt before asking the user to use it.

title: Prevent raw ids and wrong ancestry in player-facing prose
description: CLI playtest cli_takeover_haiku_20260520 exposed two immersion breaks: the narrator rendered a tavern speaker as raw id 'vesna_brem' for several lines, and Herrik addressed Lyra as an elf despite her attached sheet and /describe identifying her as a Hill Dwarf/hill dwarf cleric. Evidence in app/storage/playtest_reports/cli_takeover_haiku_20260520.log around lines 464-507 and 666-668. Acceptance: player-facing prose uses display names for spawned/implicit NPCs and respects attached D&D identity/species in narrator and NPC dialogue context.
notes: Implemented narrator guidance to convert underscore raw identifiers into best-guess display names. NPC dialogue ancestry/species grounding remains outstanding and should be handled separately.

title: Bridge narrative gear acquisition into D&D inventory or loot
description: In CLI playtest cli_takeover_haiku_20260520, Korva visibly issued rope, bedrolls, rations, torches, waterskins, food parcels, and a healer's kit. /loot stayed empty and /inventory still showed only the imported D&D Beyond equipment. From a D&D perspective, gear acquisition should either create a loot offer, update carried inventory, or explicitly tell the player it is narrative-only. Acceptance: when router/narrator awards mundane adventuring gear in a D&D session, the CLI exposes a structured inventory/loot path or a clear non-inventory explanation; /loot all should be testable on this path.
close_reason: Added a D&D-only narrative mundane gear handoff fallback that creates claimable loot offers for obvious visible supplies, strengthened router loot guidance, and tested /loot-all style claiming through inventory.

title: Add non-combat D&D checks for risky scouting and parley
description: CLI playtest cli_takeover_haiku_20260520 ran with player_roll_mode=interactive and attached sample D&D sheets. Risky scouting/listening/stealth/recon and tense parley all resolved as Cat I prose with no pending /roll prompts: Garrick scouted the mill, counted seven armed brigands, and found a covered lane; Lyra approached under cover and negotiated with a drawn bow on her, but no Stealth/Perception/Insight/Persuasion check fired. From a D&D table perspective these are obvious ability-check moments. Acceptance: D&D adapter can request interactive player rolls for non-combat exploration/social Cat II uncertainty without forcing initiative, and CLI /roll can resolve them into visible prose.
close_reason: Duplicate of ayoa-6x1; 2026-05-20 CLI rerun evidence appended there.

title: Align Unblessed opening with guild-hall premise
description: The Unblessed Summon seed premise says the opening beat should start on the third morning at the Caer Veylan Adventurers' Guild Hall, but /begin in the CLI playtest opened in the Mother Cathedral summoning chamber before later jumps to the guild hall. Verify whether this is seed context, router prompt interpretation, or checkpoint state, then align the opening with the intended first playable frame.
close_reason: Fixed router first-turn context to surface current locations, aligned Unblessed seed to the third-morning Guild Hall opening, and verified /begin via CLI in codex_unblessed_opening_ayoa_1ck.

title: Make explicit D&D skill-check requests produce dice when appropriate
description: The multiplayer CLI playtest had Lyra explicitly ask to inspect Korva, the hall, and contract papers for divine corruption, undead influence, coercion, and injuries, naming Wisdom/Insight/Religion/Medicine. The turn resolved only as narrative observation with no pending roll. Evaluate the D&D router threshold for explicit player-requested checks and add a contract that produces code-owned dice when uncertainty and sheet skills matter.
notes: 2026-05-20 longer CLI evidence: session cli_long_dnd_social_20260520 used takeover path, Garrick/Lyra sample sheets, interactive rolls, and Haiku-tier character agents. Targeted present-character checks now mostly work: Lyra Insight vs Korva opened Cat II and produced private POV facts; Garrick explicit Persuasion opened Cat II then correctly no-rolled when Korva already agreed; Stealth/Investigation, Intimidation, and Deception all opened Cat II. Remaining gap: Lyra explicitly requested a road Perception check before the mill, but router resolved Cat I with an automatic clue and /roll had no pending dice. Also, plain-language 'trying to persuade her' without the word check still stayed Cat I. See app/storage/playtest_reports/cli_long_dnd_social_20260520.tty around lines 275-280, 322-362, 407-422, and 929-971.
